assessments.reasoning: Nonlocal_kind sets DEF_NONLOCAL. Class analysis adds __class__ to the child-bound set despite withholding ordinary class bindings; analyze_name finds that entry and sets FREE when it is not a type parameter. The class then consumes the special free name to mark the class-closure need. The independent symtable classification and compiled free-variable tuple confirm that chain.

challenge.method: Traced the directive, child-bound and class-closure branches of the exact implementation. Ran symtable and compiled a direct method in a module-level class with neither a class attribute assignment to __class__ nor an enclosing function. Also tried a nonlocal directive for a different ordinary class attribute.
challenge.results: The direct method's __class__ was nonlocal and free, co_freevars contained that name, and the method returned its enclosing class. The ordinary class attribute produced SyntaxError. The reference's general nonlocal description mentions enclosing function scopes, but the candidate reports the special behavior of the pinned implementation.

limitations: The reproduction used the Python Software Foundation Windows AMD64 release build. It concerns the direct ordinary-method symbol classification and does not claim language-wide portability or behavior of customized class cells.
